sentence: This project studies how individual beating heart cells differ from one another when different genetic mutations cause the same heart disease.
This project uses genetic testing to study how hearing loss caused by genes develops over time and to find genes that change it.
This project studies how protein-carrying compartments move inside nerve cells and how that movement is controlled in the central nervous system.
This project tries to find out how support cells in the brain respond to and clear harmful proteins linked to Huntington's disease.
This project studies how a membrane protein moves vitamin A into and out of the eyes.
This project studies why immune cells stop working well in pancreatic cancer and why the tumor resists immunotherapy.
This project builds a shared resource that runs lab tests on immune responses and molecular profiles across clinical trials.
This project provides sequencing and computer tools to study how natural products change genes and the microbiome during inflammation.
This project gathers and analyzes population data on cancer risk, costs and outcomes, including differences between groups of people.
This project tries to find out how regulatory immune cells can improve the survival of kidney transplants in nonhuman primates.
This project tests whether heart fibroblasts make a growth factor that harms heart muscle cells in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
This project studies how the hippocampus keeps memories linked to cocaine over time, which can trigger craving.
This project studies how a change to a protein leads to surfactant problems and lung injury in patients on mechanical ventilation.
This project tries to find out how gene activity in Salmonella bacteria and infected host cells decides the outcome of an infection.
This project tests whether sleep helps older adults keep spatial memories, using brain recordings during sleep and immersive virtual environments.
This project tests whether pesticide spray seasons are linked to changes in mood and thinking in young people living in farming communities.
This project studies how HIV escapes broadly neutralizing antibodies in people.
This project builds mathematical models to work out how cancer cells change their metabolism to grow in a distant organ.
This project provides administrative, computer analysis and clinical sample support to each project and core in the program.
This project studies how a group of RNA-binding proteins helps decide the fate of nerve cells and how stem cells behave.
